title: अंश ५ · अध्याय ८

items.text:
गाः पालयन्तौ च पुनः सहितौ बल-केशवौ ।
भ्रममाणौ वने तस्मिन् रम्यं तालवनं गतौ ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
gāḥ pālayantau ca punaḥ sahitau bala-keśavau |
bhramamāṇau vane tasmin ramyaṃ tālavanaṃ gatau || 1 ||

items.text:
तत्तु तालवनं दिव्यं धेनुको नाम दानवः ।
मृगमांसकृताहारः सदाध्यास्ते खराकृतिः ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
tattu tālavanaṃ divyaṃ dhenuko nāma dānavaḥ |
mṛgamāṃsakṛtāhāraḥ sadādhyāste kharākṛtiḥ || 2 ||

items.text:
तत्तु तालवन पक्क-फलसम्पत्समन्वितम् ।
दृष्ट्वा स्पृहान्विता गोपाः फलादानेऽब्रु वन्, वचः ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
tattu tālavana pakka-phalasampatsamanvitam |
dṛṣṭvā spṛhānvitā gopāḥ phalādāne'bru van, vacaḥ || 3 ||

items.text:
हे राम! हे कृष्ण! सदा धेनुकेनैष रक्ष्यते ।
भूप्रदेशो यतस्तस्मात् पक्कानीमानि सन्ति वै ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
he rāma! he kṛṣṇa! sadā dhenukenaiṣa rakṣyate |
bhūpradeśo yatastasmāt pakkānīmāni santi vai || 4 ||

items.text:
फलानि पश्य तालानां गन्धामोदितदींशि च ।
वयमत्तुमभीप्सामः पात्यन्तां यदि रोचसे ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
phalāni paśya tālānāṃ gandhāmoditadīṃśi ca |
vayamattumabhīpsāmaḥ pātyantāṃ yadi rocase || 5 ||

items.text:
इति गोपकुमाराणां श्रुत्वा सङ्कर्षणो वचः ।
कृष्णश्व पातयामास भुवि तालफलानि वै ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
iti gopakumārāṇāṃ śrutvā saṅkarṣaṇo vacaḥ |
kṛṣṇaśva pātayāmāsa bhuvi tālaphalāni vai || 6 ||

items.text:
फलानां पततां शब्दमाकर्ण्य स दुरासदः ।
आजगाम सुदुष्टात्मा कोपादू दैतेयगर्द्दभः ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
phalānāṃ patatāṃ śabdamākarṇya sa durāsadaḥ |
ājagāma suduṣṭātmā kopādū daiteyagarddabhaḥ || 7 ||

items.text:
पद्भयामुभाभ्यां स तदा पश्विमाभ्यां बली बलम् ।
जघानोरसि ताभ्याञ्च स च तेनाप्यगृह्यत ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
padbhayāmubhābhyāṃ sa tadā paśvimābhyāṃ balī balam |
jaghānorasi tābhyāñca sa ca tenāpyagṛhyata || 8 ||

items.text:
गृहीत्वा भ्रामणेनैव सोऽम्बरे गतजीवितम् ।
तस्मिन्नेव च चिक्षेप वेगेन तृणराजनि ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
gṛhītvā bhrāmaṇenaiva so'mbare gatajīvitam |
tasminneva ca cikṣepa vegena tṛṇarājani || 9 ||

items.text:
ततः फलान्यनेकानि तालाग्रान्निपतन् खरः ।
पृथिव्यां पातयामास महावातोऽम्बुदानिव ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ phalānyanekāni tālāgrānnipatan kharaḥ |
pṛthivyāṃ pātayāmāsa mahāvāto'mbudāniva || 10 ||

items.text:
अन्यानप्यस्य वै ज्ञातीनागतान् दैत्यगर्द्दभान् ।
कृष्णाश्विक्षेप तालाग्र बलभद्रश्व लीलया ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
anyānapyasya vai jñātīnāgatān daityagarddabhān |
kṛṣṇāśvikṣepa tālāgra balabhadraśva līlayā || 11 ||

items.text:
क्षणेनालङ्कृता पृथ्वी पक्कस्तालफलैस्तथा ।
दैत्यगर्द्दभदेहैश्व मैत्रेय! शुशुभेऽधिकम् ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
kṣaṇenālaṅkṛtā pṛthvī pakkastālaphalaistathā |
daityagarddabhadehaiśva maitreya! śuśubhe'dhikam || 12 ||

items.text:
ततो गावो निराबाधास्तस्मिंस्तालवने द्रिज!
नवशस्य सुख चेरुर्यन्न भुक्तमभूत् पुरा ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
tato gāvo nirābādhāstasmiṃstālavane drija!
navaśasya sukha ceruryanna bhuktamabhūt purā || 13 ||

en_chapter: Parāçara said:—Thereupon again driving their cattle, Kesava and Balarāma rambled together in the forest, and on one occasion went to a pleasing grove of palms. There lived in that pleasing grove a demon named Dhenuka, resembling an ass in appearance and living upon the flesh of deer. Beholding the fruits there ripe, the cow herds, being anxious to take them, said—"O Rāma! O Krishna! Dhenuka always lives here and therefore the trees are loaded with ripe fruits the smell of which perfumes the air. We wish to eat some. Will you throw some down?" Hearing those words, Krishna and Sankarsana brought down some fruits on the ground. Hearing the sound of the falling fruits, the dreadful and malignant demon Dhenuka, having the countenance of an ass, arrived there speedily, and being angry began to kick Rāma on the breast with his hinder heels. Catching him by his both hind legs, Rāma however hurled him round till he died; then he threw up the dead body to the top of the palm tree from the branches of which it struck down enough fruits like rain drops poured down on earth by the wind. The relatives of Dhenuka came running to his help, and Krishna and Rāma did the same thing with them until the trees were filled with dead asses and the ground was covered with ripe fruits. Thenceforth the cattle grazed unobstructed in the palm groves and cropped the new pasturage where they had never gone before.
